content:
maria.g: Quick security/privacy check — proposing to change telemetry-worker request logs retention from 180d -> 90d to cut S3 costs. Logs are under s3://redwood-telemetry/logs/. Traces (Jaeger) remain at 30d. Some logs currently include hashed user_id and an ephemeral token field. Plan: backfill redact `full_email`, drop `ephemeral_token`, and then run lifecycle to delete older objects after 90d. Does this sound safe or do we need a retention-exception / formal privacy sign-off?

samir: Can you confirm whether the hashed user_id is reversible or salted? If it's just sha256(user_id) and we don't store the salt, usually OK. If it's HMAC with a customer ID or reversible mapping, we need to treat it as PII. Also any auth tokens must be fully removed, not just masked.

maria.g: The hashing is sha256(user_id + static_salt) — salt is internal but stable. We can change to HMAC with per-environment salt or drop the field entirely. For tokens the field is `ephemeral_token` and we never use it after ingestion.

samir: My preference: drop tokens entirely, and for identifiers either make them non-linkable across datasets (randomized id) or store only a truncated prefix that can't be used to re-identify. If you keep hashed ids that are linkable, we need privacy review.

alex.w: From infra side — lifecycle policy change is straightforward. Two notes: 1) if you plan a backfill redaction, do it in a deduplicated pass to avoid double-storage; 2) update the bucket IAM so only the redact-job role can write deletes for older objects. Example redact agent config (will need to adapt):

```json
{
  "redact_rules": [
    {"field": "full_email", "regex": "\\b[\\w.%+-]+@[\\w.-]+\\.[a-zA-Z]{2,}\\b", "replacement": "[REDACTED_EMAIL]"},
    {"field": "ephemeral_token", "regex": ".+", "replacement": "[REMOVED]"}
  ]
}
```

katie.p: Privacy flag: if after redaction there is no PII (email, phone, un-hashed identifiers) and tokens removed, 90d is fine. However — because current logs may have linkable hashed IDs we need a short privacy review: please attach 10 sample rows (anonymized) and the backfill plan. If you intend to keep the stable hashed id, we treat that as pseudonymous data and need to document purpose & retention in the data inventory. If you drop it, no extra exception needed.

maria.g: OK — will produce anonymized samples and the backfill script. Quick Q: does removing `ephemeral_token` in-place count as deletion for compliance, or do we need S3 object rewrite + delete?

samir: You need to rewrite objects (or produce redacted copies) and then delete original objects. S3 lifecycle delete alone won't help if originals still accessible. Also rotate any KMS keys used for logs if they allowed long-term access.

sec-bot: Created ticket PRIV-2102 with summary "telemetry-worker log retention change: 180d->90d" and linked required reviewers: @samir @katie.p. Please attach samples to the ticket.

devops-oncall: Ping for deployment window — we should schedule the backfill during low traffic and limit concurrent list/gets to avoid S3 throttling. Also add me to the PR for runbook / rollback steps.

maria.g: Will open PR with backfill + redact job + lifecycle policy. Tagging reviewers: @samir @katie.p @alex.w @devops-oncall. PR link: https://git.redwood.dev/telemetry/telemetry-worker/pull/324 (draft) — I'll include anonymized samples in the PR and attach PRIV-2102. ETA for draft tomorrow EOD. :+1:

samir: Sounds good — will review once draft has samples and the IAM change. Please add a one-liner in the PR describing why we chose 90d (cost analysis + no PII post-redact).

maria.g: will do, thanks everyone!
